messages.subject: Re: Creating annotationData/ directories?
parts:
Hi, I will take the freedom to forward this question to the mailing
list. Please send *all* questions to the mailing list, because...

"FAQ. 2008-03-26: Why do you not want to answer questions sent to your
private email address?

A: Please post all questions related to aroma.affymetrix to the
aroma-af...@googlegroups.com mailing list. This way there is a
chance that others also can help out with your problem/question, which
means that you hopefully get a reply quicker. All questions and
answers are archived and searchable online. Because of this, we can
then refer to already answered questions by replying with a link.
Moreover, this way the chances for finding answers online increase.
So, please understand this when I ask you to repost your question to
the mailing list. It will not only save me but everyone a lot of
time."

URL: http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/frequently-asked-questions

More comments below...

On Tue, Apr 1, 2008 at 11:11 AM, Gao Zhang <gzh...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Dr.Bengtsson,
>
> Hi! I am following the thread on the page of
> http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/total-copy-number-analysis
> for set-up.
>
> My affy data is of Affy 250K Sty type so I figured I should put:
>
> Mapping250K_Sty.cdf
> Mapping250K_Sty,na24,HB20080214.ugp, and
> Mapping250K_Sty,na24,HB20080214.ufl
>
> in the folder called 'annotationData/chipTypes/Mapping250K_Sty'.
>
> But I did not find the folder of 'chipTypes' under the 'annotationData'.
> Should
> I manually create these folders? I found the folder 'annotationData' as the
> path of:
>
> C:\Program Files\R\R-2.6.2\library\aroma.affymetrix\annotationData
>
> Please direct me how to do this. I am new to R so sorry for these naive
> questions.

Yes, you have to create those directories yourself.

[The annotationData/ is created as a "side effect" when
aroma.affymetrix tries to locate it and it does not exist.]

Also, you do *not* want to have:

C:\Program Files\R\R-2.6.2\library\aroma.affymetrix\

as your working directory (trust me on that one). Instead, make sure
to use another working directory, e.g. under 'C:/...../My
Documents/AffymetrixAnalysis/' in which you create directories (with
subdirectories):

annotationData/
rawData/

Then you can use setwd() in your script to set the working directory
to be C:/...../My Documents/AffymetrixAnalysis/.

Cheers

/Henrik
